channel.title: DIPT - SE Research Monitor
channel.description: Newly approved Software Engineering research, summarised and scored for industrial relevance.

item.title: Kerncap: Automated Kernel Extraction and Isolation for AMD GPUs
item.description: Practitioners can significantly accelerate GPU performance engineering by replacing brittle manual extraction with a single-command automated workflow. The generated self-contained reproducers also serve as essential infrastructure for autotuning agents and LLM-driven kernel generators requiring rapid, isolated evaluation.

item.title: TSCG: Deterministic Tool-Schema Compilation for Agentic LLM Deployments
item.description: Practitioners can deploy local small models as functional agents by using TSCG to overcome JSON parsing limitations, effectively democratizing agentic capabilities. The tool offers a zero-dependency TypeScript implementation with specific optimization profiles tailored to different model architectures, ensuring reliable performance without requiring expensive frontier API calls.

item.title: Mitigating False Positives in Static Memory Safety Analysis of Rust Programs via Reinforcement Learning
item.description: This method significantly reduces warning fatigue and manual review overhead for developers working with unsafe Rust code in safety-critical domains. By substantially lowering false positives while maintaining high recall, it enhances the reliability and adoption of automated static analysis tools in industrial software engineering workflows.

item.title: Firmware Distribution as Attack Surface: A Security Study of ASIC Cryptocurrency Miners
item.description: Practitioners must recognize that firmware update packages themselves constitute a significant attack surface, allowing attackers to derive detailed architectural knowledge and exploit paths without owning the hardware. This highlights an urgent need to secure the firmware distribution lifecycle and upgrade protocols like Stratum V2 to prevent revenue redirection and device takeover in mining operations.

item.title: Less Is More: Engineering Challenges of On-Device Small Language Model Integration in a Mobile Application
item.description: Practitioners can achieve viable offline AI features by accepting that on-device SLMs require radical scope reduction and defensive parsing rather than optimistic trust in model outputs. The study highlights that shifting inference to the edge eliminates recurring cloud API costs and provides a structural privacy guarantee, making it an economically and ethically sustainable alternative for scalable mobile applications.

item.title: Vulnerability Identification by Harnessing Inter-connected Multi-Source Information
item.description: This approach enables timely security alerts for downstream developers by automatically detecting silent vulnerability patches in open-source dependencies before official releases. By improving the accuracy of vulnerability identification and classification, it helps practitioners mitigate risks associated with unpatched third-party components more effectively.

item.title: Code Broker: A Multi-Agent System for Automated Code Quality Assessment
item.description: Code Broker offers a practical workflow to reduce the latency and cost of defect remediation by providing rapid, quantitative assessments that bridge the gap between shallow linting and slow human review. Its modular design allows for integration into developer workflows, potentially alleviating bottlenecks where senior engineers spend excessive time on code reviews.

item.title: Do Agents Dream of Root Shells? Partial-Credit Evaluation of LLM Agents in Capture the Flag Challenges
item.description: Practitioners should recognize that while LLM agents can make partial progress on security tasks, they currently lack the perseverance and memory required for reliable autonomous exploitation. This highlights the need for improved hierarchical planning and explicit memory systems before deploying such agents in critical automated software testing or security auditing pipelines.

item.title: Autoregressive, Yet Revisable: In Decoding Revision for Secure Code Generation
item.description: Practitioners can achieve higher code security without the latency and token costs associated with multi-turn agentic workflows or external static analysis tools. The framework allows for real-time, in-context correction of vulnerabilities during generation, streamlining the development pipeline. This approach demonstrates that internalizing revision loops is a viable strategy for enhancing LLM reliability in safety-critical software engineering tasks.

item.title: In Line with Context: Repository-Level Code Generation via Context Inlining
item.description: Practitioners can leverage this framework to improve the accuracy of AI-assisted coding tools by providing more precise, dependency-aware context rather than relying on generic similarity searches. The approach offers a scalable solution for handling large codebases, ensuring that generated code aligns with existing repository conventions and architectural constraints.

item.title: Experience converting a large mathematical software package written in C++ to C++20 modules
item.description: Practitioners can adopt a hybrid approach by providing both header and module interfaces from a single codebase to maintain compatibility while gradually modernizing. The work suggests that a 'bottom-up' conversion strategy, starting with foundational libraries, is more viable than a top-down approach for the mathematical software ecosystem due to complex dependency webs.

item.title: Software Engineering for Self-Adaptive Robotics: A Research Agenda
item.description: Practitioners can utilize this agenda to guide the development of reliable autonomous systems in sectors like industrial automation, search-and-rescue, and assistive robotics. The proposed roadmap provides actionable insights for integrating digital twins and AI-driven adaptation to meet real-world deployment complexities.

item.title: Search-Based Software Engineering and AI Foundation Models: Current Landscape and Future Roadmap
item.description: Practitioners can leverage this roadmap to understand how to integrate foundation models with established search-based optimization techniques for improved automation and decision-making. It offers guidance on addressing current limitations in AI-driven software engineering through hybrid approaches. The insights help industries anticipate future trends and opportunities in areas such as automated testing, code generation, and system design.

item.title: Lightweight Vulnerability Detection from Code Metrics and Token Features
item.description: This lightweight approach offers a computationally efficient solution for nightly scans or pull-request gating where thousands of functions must be scored quickly on standard hardware. Practitioners can use these transparent models to prioritize human review by ranking functions, though they must account for limited cross-project transferability and potential leakage from comments.

item.title: EngThrive: Make It Fast and Easy to Do Great Work
item.description: Practitioners should adopt a multi-dimensional measurement approach using surveys and basic telemetry to identify bottlenecks without needing perfect data immediately. By focusing on continuous improvement across Speed, Ease, Quality, and Thriving, organizations can make evidence-based decisions about tools, policies, and organizational structures that genuinely enhance developer effectiveness.

item.title: Root-Cause-Driven Automated Vulnerability Repair
item.description: Practitioners can leverage Kumushi to reduce the backlog of disclosed vulnerabilities by generating higher-quality patches that are less likely to leave exploitable defects unresolved. The study highlights the necessity of moving beyond simple test oracles to expert-informed evaluation methods for ensuring the reliability and security of automated repair tools in production environments.

item.title: A Multi-Agent Consensus Protocol for Stable Software Remodularization
item.description: Practitioners can use this approach to mathematically enforce stability budgets, preventing architectural erosion that imposes high cognitive burdens on development teams. This provides a principled mechanism for balancing structural quality against maintenance costs without relying on arbitrary heuristic weights.

item.title: Semantic Reverse Engineering Legacy Software Applications with ChatGPT, Gemini AI, and Claude AI
item.description: Practitioners should not rely on free or standard versions of these AI tools for semantic reverse engineering of legacy systems, as they may generate plausible but incorrect interpretations of business logic. The study suggests that human expertise, particularly in mathematics and formal logic, remains essential for validating AI outputs when dealing with complex legacy codebases.

item.title: Neuro-Symbolic Agents for Hallucination-Free Requirements Reuse
item.description: Practitioners can deploy this model-agnostic framework to automate requirements elicitation while guaranteeing regulatory compliance and logical consistency through hard-coded symbolic enforcement. The approach offers a scalable solution for reducing development effort in software product lines by bridging the gap between vague stakeholder intent and rigorous formal models.

item.title: LLM-Guided Issue Generation from Uncovered Code Segments
item.description: Practitioners can use this tool to automatically prioritize and triage latent defects in untested code, significantly reducing the manual effort required for bug discovery and verification. By surfacing high-impact issues like security vulnerabilities and data-loss bugs directly from uncovered segments, it helps developers focus on the most critical quality assurance tasks first.

item.title: Addressing Methodological Sensitivity in MCDM with a Systematic Pipeline Approach to Data Transformation Sensitivity Analysis
item.description: Practitioners should adopt this systematic approach for high-impact decisions like strategic investments or public policy where transparency and auditability are essential. The framework enables the identification of robust alternatives and provides interpretable sensitivity bounds, though it is less suitable for operational decisions requiring immediate responses due to computational overhead.

item.title: SysLLMatic: Large Language Models are Software System Optimizers
item.description: This approach offers a practical path toward 'push-button' optimization, allowing engineers to significantly improve system speed, reduce operating costs, and enhance energy efficiency with minimal manual effort. By automating the identification and resolution of performance bottlenecks, it supports sustainable computing practices and reduces the resource burden typically associated with deep performance tuning.

item.title: Detecting Vulnerabilities in Encrypted Software Code while Ensuring Code Privacy
item.description: Software companies can safely outsource security testing to third parties without risking intellectual property theft or exposing sensitive source code. This enables the adoption of specialized external analysis services within DevSecOps pipelines, balancing rigorous vulnerability detection with strict data privacy requirements.

item.title: Two Integration Pathways in Human-Centered Requirements Engineering: A Systematic Mapping Study of Structural Gaps
item.description: Practitioners should recognize that current human-centered techniques are largely siloed in early requirements phases, creating a gap between user experience insights and formal system specifications. The findings establish an empirical foundation for Experience-Centered Requirements Engineering (XCRE), urging the industry to operationalize user experience as a first-class concern throughout the entire development lifecycle rather than just during initial elicitation.

item.title: From SWE-ZERO to SWE-HERO: Execution-free to Execution-based Fine-tuning for Software Engineering Agents
item.description: Practitioners can deploy smaller, more cost-effective open-source agents that bypass the brittle infrastructure requirements of Docker-based environments during training. The framework enables scalable data collection from a wider range of real-world repositories and supports efficient test-time scaling to improve resolution rates without proportional increases in training complexity.

item.title: SWE Context Bench: A Benchmark for Context Learning in Coding
item.description: Practitioners should prioritize robust summarization and adaptive retrieval mechanisms to maximize the efficiency of coding agents in production environments. Implementing structured context management and filtering strategies can reduce computational costs while maintaining high resolution accuracy. Agents must be designed to distinguish between useful insights and misleading details in imperfect historical data.

item.title: Exploring the Output of Software Testing Tools through a Visual Comparative Analysis
item.description: Developers of testing tools can use these findings to design more consistent and effective visual interfaces for both CLI and GUI environments. By adopting identified trends, tool creators can improve the seamless experience for testers and reduce cognitive load through better information hierarchy and interactivity.

item.title: LCM: Lossless Context Management
item.description: Practitioners can deploy reliable infinite-context architectures today without waiting for models to master meta-skills of memory management, as LCM offers zero-cost continuity for short tasks and deterministic scaling for long ones. The architecture reduces the variance penalty associated with stochastic model behavior, enabling more robust production coding agents that maintain lossless retrievability of prior state.
